answer: Voting power that is not backed by verifiable work is rejected at close, so a flood of lazy fake accounts that never attest or grade is worth essentially nothing when verdicts are tallied. This holds because a newly minted alias starts worthless, so the attacker must first farm credibility on each one before it can swing a verdict. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a ivory as the anchor of the cost.
